notes: COLD RUN 9071. The club brief an eighth time, deliberately unchanged from 9070's so the only new variable is the tools. THE DEFECT THIS TESTS: the walker descended a ladder on 9070's package and the floor below read grey and untextured from above, with the real texture appearing on the way down -- then the same on a staircase. Theming skins a slab's TOP as a floor and its BOTTOM as a ceiling and never touches the faces a hole cut through it CREATES, so deli_counter._slab_holes_cut leaves a floor_thick-deep ring of flat gb_floor around every ladder shaft and stairwell: 1.44 m2 around a 1.10 x 1.30 m opening, the same area as the opening itself, 10.44 m2 over 8 cut slabs in 9070's package. Four cheaper explanations were measured and refuted first (not draw distance, not occlusion culling, not z-fighting, not a gap in the floor) and it predates the performance work -- every package back to 2026-09-11 ships gb_floor on its slabs -- so that pass revealed it rather than causing it. LF 0.106.0 adds _skin_slabs beside _skin_stairs (world triplanar, because a boolean's new faces carry no usable UVs) and a greybox_skin gate that counts surfaces still drawing a gb_* material in the running scene, refusing on slabs and reporting the rest. WHAT WOULD FALSIFY THE CLAIM: a package whose census still reports slab surfaces on a greybox material, a worldskin push_error naming a base it could not find a pack for, or a walk that still shows a grey collar around an opening -- a gate that passes is not the same as a level that reads right.
